note: Public-method parity for the UCT RS VARS columns (engineering map 2026-11-08 unit 3-13; plan §12.1; KB 01-methodologies §9), read by tests/test_rs_phase3_parity.py against api/services/relative_strength.vars_columns. The map asks for 'matches the OANDA case study's sign changes on its dates'. The page does NOT publish enough to do that: every VARS reading is in a chart image (Figs. 2-6, TradingView screenshots), the text states no date of a zero-line or moving-average crossing, and no price or VARS series is given as text. `published.sign_changes` is therefore empty and `reproducible` is false, so the sign-change test is a strict xfail with that reason, never a pass. What the page DOES publish as text, and what is checked: the parameters (SPY benchmark, daily bars, ATR 20, lookback 60, 50-bar SMA of VARS) and the four state conditions. The two case studies' dated facts are kept under `case_studies` for the record; they are price facts and undated chart readings, not VARS sign changes, so nothing is asserted on them. To make the sign-change test real, fill `published.sign_changes` (each {date, from_sign, to_sign}) and `price_series` from a source that states them as text, then set `reproducible` to true.

reference.title: VARS: How to prevent the high-beta trap and find the relevant stocks
reference.author: Kelvin Wong (Senior Market Analyst)
reference.transcribed: Parameters, the formula's structure, the four state conditions, and the dated price facts of the two case studies. No VARS values (none are given as text).

published.formula: ShareChg_t = (C_t − C_t−1) / ATR_t (the share's own ATR, per bar); IndexChg_t the same on the benchmark with the benchmark's own ATR; VARS = Σ ShareChg − Σ IndexChg over the lookback

case_studies.vars_reading: bearish divergence: a lower VARS high above its 50-bar MA (undated, chart only)
